title: You Are My Refuge
superscription: A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

verses.text: I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift my voice to the LORD for mercy.
I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him.
Although my spirit grows faint within me, You know my way. Along the path I travel they have hidden a snare for me.
Look to my right and see; no one attends to me. There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul.
I cry to You, O LORD: "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."
Listen to my cry, for I am brought quite low. Rescue me from my pursuers, for they are too strong for me.
Free my soul from prison, that I may praise Your name. The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me.

context.author: The title says “A Maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.” The cave may be Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1) or the cave at En Gedi where he spared Saul (1 Samuel 24:3). Psalm 57 has the same setting.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.mapLabel: THE CAVE: ADULLAM OR EN GEDI
context.setting: “I cry aloud to the LORD; I lift my voice to the LORD for mercy. I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him” (vv.1-2). David is hunted and alone: “Look to my right and see; no one attends to me. There is no refuge for me; no one cares for my soul” (v.4). So he turns to God: “You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living” (v.5). “Free my soul from prison, that I may praise Your name. The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me” (v.7).
context.custom: The right hand was where a defender or advocate stood (Psalm 16:8; 109:31), so “no one attends to me” at the right means no one to help. The cave felt like a prison (v.7). At Adullam “all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him” (1 Samuel 22:2), as v.7 hopes.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 143: Do not bring Your servant into judgment.
context.timelineBible: Paul wrote at his trial, “no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me… But the Lord stood by me” (2 Timothy 4:16-17). Jesus invites, “Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened” (Matthew 11:28).

otBackground.note: In the shadow of Your wings.

overview.summary: Hiding in a cave with no one to help, David pours out his complaint to the LORD, his only refuge and portion, and asks to be freed so the righteous can gather round him in praise.
overview.settingLine: A fugitive’s prayer in the dark.

customs.t: Common hiding places in the Judean hills.

archaeology.t: Limestone caves around Adullam used as shelters and hideouts for millennia.
Caves above the oasis, used in many periods.

overview.discussion: “no one cares for my soul” (v.4). When I feel alone, what does it mean to call God my portion?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
